country.comment: Examines 53 municipalities in the departments of Caldas, Quindío and Risaralda in Colombia.
country.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 6, Catastro y SGP; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos (Figura 1)

effect_estimate.comment: Cadastral updating in isolation did not uniformly raise property tax collection, SGP water/sanitation transfers, piped water coverage (significant in only 15.15% of municipalities), or drinking water quality, although sewerage subscribers and coverage increased significantly in 66.67% of studied municipalities.
effect_estimate.value: Using municipality-specific robust paired-samples t-tests comparing the 5-year period up to cadastral updating against the subsequent 5-year period (alpha = 0.05), significant post-updating increases were found for: total property tax collection in 27/53 municipalities (50.94%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.80) and per capita property tax in 29/53 (54.72%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.69); national SGP water and basic sanitation transfers in 13/52 municipalities (25.00%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.81); piped water (acueducto) subscribers in 8/33 municipalities (24.24%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.77) and water proxy coverage (subscribers/cadastral parcels) in 5/33 municipalities (15.15%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.82); and sewerage (alcantarillado) subscribers in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56) and sewerage proxy coverage in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56). The Water Quality Risk Index (IRCA) increased significantly (reflecting higher risk or expanded sanitary sampling) in 12/42 municipalities (28.57%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.87), with no significant change in 30/42 (71.43%).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF pp. 9–16, Resultados and Tablas 2–7; PDF p. 17, Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented statistical association): the study reports pre-post statistical comparisons across secondary municipal datasets with Serious/Critical ROBINS-I confounding risk (precluding 3) and explicitly notes in the limitations (PDF p. 17) the lack of detailed process evidence explaining why or how cadastral updates translated (or failed to translate) into tax collection and utility coverage changes (precluding 2).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF pp. 11, 16–17, Resultados and Conclusiones

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines municipal cadastral updating of urban/rural parcels and property tax assessment/collection (property), spatial/parcel data for local utility planning, socioeconomic stratification, and SSPD coverage certification toward a multipurpose cadastre (planning), and national-to-municipal intergovernmental SGP water and basic sanitation fiscal transfers (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5–6, Impuesto Predial and Catastro y SGP; PDF pp. 11, 17, Resultados and Conclusiones

outcome_flags.comment: Measures registered utility subscribers for piped water and sewerage (formal_connection, water_access, sanitation_access), proxy coverage defined as subscribers divided by cadastral parcels (service_coverage), and drinking water quality via the Water Quality Risk Index IRCA (service_quality).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 6–7, Metodología y Datos (Fórmula 1); PDF pp. 13–16, Tablas 5–7

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Evaluates a specific non-randomized administrative intervention (municipal cadastral updating implemented across staggered years 2004–2015) using longitudinal pre-intervention (5-year Periodo 1) vs. post-intervention (5-year Periodo 2) comparisons. Because it uses uncontrolled within-municipality pre-post paired t-tests without an untreated comparator group or adjustment for secular trends and concurrent municipal reforms, overall ROBINS-I risk of bias is Serious/Critical.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1

sample_size.comment: While the text reports analyzing 53 (property tax), 52 (SGP), 33 (water/sewerage), and 42 (IRCA) municipalities, printed Tables 2, 3, 4, and 7 display 42, 42, 42, and 41 municipality rows respectively due to table truncation in the journal layout; Table 1 lists all 53 municipalities and Tables 5–6 list all 33 water/sewerage municipalities.
sample_size.value: 53 municipalities across 3 departments (Caldas, Quindío and Risaralda) observed over two 5-year periods (10 years per municipality within 2000–2020; analytical subsamples: 53 municipalities for property tax, 52 for SGP water/sanitation transfers, 33 for water and sewerage subscribers/coverage, and 42 for IRCA water quality)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1; PDF pp. 11, 16, Resultados

study_design.comment: Compares annual municipal observations across two 5-year windows—up to and including the year of cadastral updating (Periodo 1) vs. the 5 years following updating (Periodo 2)—separately for each municipality using Yuen/Mair-Wilcox Robust Paired Samples T-Tests in JAMOVI (Walrus library), without an untreated control group or multivariable regression controls.
study_design.value: Observational pre-post (before-and-after) longitudinal municipal panel study using robust paired-samples t-tests (two 5-year periods before vs. after cadastral updating)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1
